title: She grew up in a small Haryana town dreaming of flight. On this day, she left the atmosphere. November 19, 2026.
excerpt: On the anniversary of her first launch, the story of Kalpana Chawla's path from Karnal, Haryana to the flight deck of Space Shuttle Columbia.
bodyHtml:
She grew up in a small Haryana town dreaming of flight. On this day, she left the atmosphere

On November 19, 1997, Kalpana Chawla launched aboard Space Shuttle Columbia on mission STS-87, becoming the first India-born woman in space. Chawla was born and raised in Karnal, Haryana, where she earned her aeronautical engineering degree at Punjab Engineering College before moving to the US for graduate study. STS-87 was her first of two spaceflights.

A small-town engineering degree carried her all the way to orbit. Chawla logged over 372 hours in space across her two missions. She remains one of the most widely recognized symbols of what an Indian engineering education can lead to, inspiring a generation of students toward science and space careers.

Chawla's path - small-town India to a Space Shuttle flight deck - is still the reference point for what's possible when that ambition is matched with the right training.
